strengths: The paper addresses a highly practical and complex real-world challenge—connecting digital, map-based exploration with on-site, camera-aware spatial reasoning and navigation.

The proposed grid-aligned map representation is simple yet effective, enabling multimodal LLMs to easily align visual map regions with external geospatial indexes, leading to a massive boost in POI detection accuracy (from ~43% to ~90%).

The custom distillation pipeline—which distills spatial reasoning from GPT-4o into a lightweight Florence-2 model using 2D/3D visual cues (YOLO-World, Depth Anything V2)—is a very solid engineering design that successfully achieves low latency (1.7s vs. 12.4s).
The backend multi-agent architecture successfully integrates localization, navigation, and spatial understanding into a cohesive and interpretable system.
weaknesses: Several key quantitative results in Section IV.D (e.g., 84% accuracy vs. Florence-VL's 27%, object recall of 7 vs. 4, and latency comparisons) are presented entirely in the text. Organizing these comparative results into a structured table (including columns for Accuracy, Latency, Recall, and Parameter size) would significantly improve the clarity of the evaluation section.

The spatial understanding evaluation relies on OpenAI's o1 model as a judge. LLM-as-a-judge protocols can suffer from systematic biases. More details are needed regarding how the grading prompt was structured and whether any human verification was conducted to measure the alignment between o1 and human annotators.

The dataset of 4,300 queries used to evaluate Maps Plus was synthetically generated using GPT-4o. Since GPT-4o or similar LLMs also form the backbone of the baselines, there is a risk of synthetic query bias. Supplementing this evaluation with a small, human-annotated query test set would strengthen the validation.

The paper is missing details regarding code, dataset, or prompt template release. Given the complexity of the pipeline (including multiple APIs, custom distillation datasets, XGBoost features, and multi-agent frameworks), sharing these resources is highly crucial for reproducibility.

strengths: Compelling system-level integration of vision-language models, geospatial APIs, and multi-agent systems for interactive travel and map assistant applications.

The proposed method for distilling spatial-reasoning capabilities from large models (GPT-4o) into a smaller, real-time edge model (Florence-2) using YOLO-World and Depth Anything V2 is a practical pipeline to reduce latency (from 12.4s to 1.7s).
Clear real-world utility and well-illustrated user interfaces/scenarios (e.g., the last-100m navigation assistance shown in Figures 10 and 11).
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: The work is primarily an engineering and integration effort combining pre-existing tools and models (GPT-4o, Florence-2, CLIP, XGBoost, YOLO-World, Depth Anything V2, Azure Maps API). The individual techniques used, such as grid overlays for spatial localization and multi-agent coordination, are standard in recent LLM-based agent frameworks.

Weak and potentially biased evaluations: In Table I, the Maps Plus component is evaluated on 4,300 queries synthetically generated by GPT-4o and queried using GPT-4o. This self-evaluation on synthetic data might skew the results. The baselines (Single Model, Model+Location) are also fundamentally disadvantaged as they do not have access to any external geospatial index.

Small-scale quantitative evaluation: The XGBoost ranker (Table II) is trained on only 500 image queries and evaluated on an extremely small test set of 50 queries. This is insufficient to draw statistically robust conclusions about the ranking model's performance.

Lack of rigour in the Spatial Reasoning evaluation: The spatial reasoning accuracy is evaluated using an LLM-as-a-judge protocol with OpenAI o1 on 400 images. Evaluating open-ended text with another LLM can be subjective, noisy, and biased towards models that mimic the teacher's (GPT-4o) output style. More standard, objective, and reproducible spatial reasoning benchmarks should be used.

Reproducibility concerns: The datasets used for training and evaluating Maps Plus, the XGBoost ranker, and the spatial understanding model are proprietary or custom-built. No code, datasets, or detailed prompt templates are provided, making it very difficult for the community to reproduce or build upon the results.

strengths: Comprehensive and Practical System Design: IMAIA successfully integrates map-based reasoning (Maps Plus) and real-world egocentric perception (PAISA) into a cohesive multi-agent assistant, bridging the gap between digital maps and physical exploration.

Efficient Spatial Understanding Model: The distillation of a lightweight Florence-2 model from GPT-4o using structured priors (depth, 2D bounding boxes) is well-thought-out, leading to a substantial 7.3x speedup and making it highly suitable for real-time edge/mobile deployment.

Multimodal Feature Fusion for Localization: The venue retrieval pipeline leverages a robust ranking framework (XGBoost) combining image-text embeddings, geodesic distance, user heading, and popularity indicators, rather than relying on standard single-modality retrievers.
Clear Presentation: The manuscript is well-written with clear diagrams (such as Figures 3, 5, 8, and 9) explaining the system workflow and user experience.
weaknesses: Limited and Synthetically Biased Evaluation: For the Maps Plus evaluation, the 4,300 queries are synthetically generated using GPT-4o. Testing with synthetic data generated by the same class of LLMs used in the system can lead to evaluation bias and may not reflect genuine human map interaction patterns. Furthermore, the evaluation dataset for venue candidate ranking is extremely small, consisting of only 50 held-out image queries.

Reliance on LLM-as-a-Judge: The spatial understanding evaluation heavily relies on OpenAI o1 to judge the accuracy of generated spatial descriptions. LLM-as-a-judge can exhibit biases, and the paper does not provide a correlation study or validation against human annotations to confirm the reliability of this metric.

Lack of Dataset and Reproducibility Details: The source of the 40,000 street-view images used for distilling the spatial understanding model is not explicitly mentioned (e.g., licensing, geographic distribution). This hinders reproducibility.

Incremental Architectural Novelty: While the system integration is impressive, the individual components rely on standard off-the-shelf modules (GPT-4o, Florence-2, CLIP, YOLO-World, Depth Anything V2, Azure Maps API). The core scientific novelty in terms of model architecture or learning algorithms is somewhat limited as it mostly aggregates existing APIs and foundational models.
